profile.stagger_pattern: Odd-year elections only. Mayor + Wards 1, 2 and 4 elected together (2019, 2023); Wards 3, 5 and 6 elected together (2021, 2025). Council size constant at 7 (Mayor + six wards) across 2019-2026. Charter Prop 408 (Nov 2018), which would have moved Tucson to even-year elections and extended sitting terms by one year, was DEFEATED 66,699 to 91,513 - so the odd-year calendar is unchanged across the whole panel.
profile.election_month: November (general, odd years); partisan primary in August
profile.notes: UNUSUAL FEATURE ESTABLISHED FROM SOURCE: council members are nominated by ward in the August primary but elected CITYWIDE in the November general. Proven directly from primary sources rather than asserted: (a) the Nov 2019 city-wide canvass gives every ward contest the same city-wide denominator (Contest Totals ~99,000 for Wards 1, 2 and 4 alike); (b) the city's own Ward-1-only report for the same election (ward_total_canvass.pdf) shows Ward 1's own electorate cast only 13,315 ballots and voted on the Ward 2 and Ward 4 contests as well; (c) the Pima County Nov 2025 summary gives Wards 3, 5 and 6 an identical city-wide Contest Total of 91,672. A ward's own voters therefore do not determine its councilmember. Seats are nonetheless labelled by ward. A.R.S. 9-821.01(D) TRAP CHECKED AND FOUND NOT TO APPLY: Tucson's August election is a PARTISAN PARTY PRIMARY, not a nonpartisan election capable of electing outright - the 2021 primary canvass prints contests as 'DEM Council Member Ward 3' and 'REP Council Member Ward 3', i.e. it nominates party candidates. No seat was decided in August in any panel year; every seat appears on the November ballot. Unopposed candidates are NOT suppressed either: Selina Barajas faced only write-ins in Nov 2025 and still appears on the certified results with full vote counts. So in Tucson an absent seat really would be missing data. Terms begin the first Monday in December after the election (2019-12-02, 2021-12-06, 2023-12-04, 2025-12-01 - all verified Mondays; the 2025 ceremonial inauguration was held the following day, Tue 2025-12-02). The Vice Mayor is an internal office selected by the council from among its members for a one-year term (formerly rotated on nine-month terms); it is tracked here as its own seat and its holder simultaneously holds a ward seat.

tenures.notes: In office before the panel window (mayor since 2011); start_date truncated to panel start. Named as Mayor on the 'City of Tucson Officials' page of the FY2019 ACFR (as of 2019-06-30).

Elected mayor 2019-11-05 (55,654 votes, 55.90%); re-elected 2023-11-07 (57,559) per the Pima County consolidated-election summary. One continuous run recorded rather than two term rows, to avoid a duplicate panel row for 2023.

Held Ward 1 before the panel window; her Ward 1 term expired at the same December 2019 handover at which she took office as mayor, so this is term_end and not an elevation-caused vacancy - Ward 1 was on the 2019 ballot in the ordinary course.
In office before the panel window; re-elected 2019-11-05 (59,513) and 2023-11-07 (59,972). Continuous throughout 2019-2026.

Elected Ward 3 in 2017; resigned effective 5:00 p.m. Monday 2021-03-01 (day-of-week checked: 2021-03-01 was a Monday). NOTE THE ACFR FAILURE MODE: the FY2021 ACFR (as of 2021-06-30) still prints PAUL DURHAM in Ward Three three months after he left - a stale carry-over, not evidence he was still serving. The dated primary/news record wins.

Appointed by the Mayor and Council at a special meeting on 2021-03-01 to serve the remainder of Durham's term (she had previously held the same Ward 3 seat 2005-2017). Corroborated by the Arizona Daily Star's 2021-12-06 inauguration report: 'Dahl is replacing Councilwoman Karin Uhlich in Ward 3, who took office earlier this year to replace former Councilman Paul Durham after his resignation.'

Won the DEM Ward 3 primary 2021-08-03 (4,031 to 2,587) and the November general; inaugurated Monday 2021-12-06. Named 'Kevin Dahl / Ward Three' on the FY2022 ACFR officials page. Re-elected citywide 2025-11-04 (60,964 to 28,765).
Named 'SHIRLEY SCOTT / Ward Four' on the FY2019 ACFR officials page (as of 2019-06-30); succeeded by Nikki Lee at the 2019-12-02 handover.

On the council since 2009; re-elected 2021 (unopposed in the DEM primary, 3,642 of 3,709 votes cast, then the November general). Announced retirement 2025-04-11 for health reasons, effective 2025-05-01, seven months before his term would have ended. Appears on the FY2019, FY2020, FY2021, FY2022 and FY2024 ACFR officials pages in Ward Five.

Appointed and sworn in Tuesday 2025-05-06 (day-of-week verified) to fill the balance of Fimbres's term; the report states explicitly that he would 'serve until Dec. 1, 2025'. Ward 5 was vacant 2025-05-01 to 2025-05-05.
Elected citywide 2025-11-04 with 65,812 votes against write-ins only. Sworn in with the new council; the Arizona Daily Star's inauguration report names her as one of the two new members.

Ward 6 since 2009; re-elected 2021 and appears in Ward Six on the FY2019-FY2022 ACFR officials pages. Announced 2024-03-11/12 that he would resign at the end of the month to take a Pima County job; resignation effective 2024-03-31, twenty months before his term expired.

Second appointment for the same person to a different ward: appointed unanimously to Ward 6 on Monday 2024-05-06 (KOLD/13 News, published 2024-05-06 22:05 MST). DATE CORRECTION: the KOLD article body says 'On Monday, April 6' - 2024-04-06 was a SATURDAY, and the story was published on Monday 2024-05-06, so the body date is a reporting error; 2024-05-06 is the correct date. Independently corroborated at high confidence by the FY2024 ACFR officials page (as of 2024-06-30), which prints 'KARIN UHLICH / Ward Six'. Ward 6 was vacant 2024-04-01 to 2024-05-05. Uhlich did not seek election in 2025.
Elected citywide 2025-11-04, 60,404 to 29,280. Described as 'newly sworn-in Ward 6 Councilmember' in the Arizona Daily Star's report on the December 2025 organizational meeting.

The date on which she was selected was not sourced, so the start is deliberately conservative and 2020 is filed as a gap rather than inferred.
Selected unanimously at the 2021-12-06 inaugural meeting 'for the next year'; end date is the implied one-year term, not a dated record.

Observed window from the city's own Ward 3 newsletters, all headed 'Vice Mayor Kevin Dahl's Ward 3 News and Updates': 2024-01-26, 2024-03-15, 2024-06-28, 2024-10-25 and 2025-01-10. Boundaries are first/last observation, not a selection record.

LOW because only the fact of her holding it during 2025 is sourced, not the start date. run_log.detail: Read agent-brief.md and the Arizona section plus cross-state findings of state-registry.md.

REGISTRY ENTRY CONFIRMED: pima.gov/2865/Election-Results is fully open to plain curl and carries City of Tucson municipal races. Caveat for the registry - the page's older-year tabs are driven by a client-side widget; the '?contentId=' links in the markup are NOT server-rendered, every one of 18 returns byte-identical HTML showing only 2024-2026. One tool call was wasted proving that. Only 2022-2026 assets are reachable from the page markup. Pulled the Nov 2023 summary (asset 38d95763) and Nov 2025 summary (asset 5595d00e) as clean text-layer PDFs; both fully source their cycles.

Tucson ran its own 2019 and 2021 municipal elections (it only joined the Pima consolidated election from 2023), so 2019/2021 had to come from the City Clerk. www.tucsonaz.gov returns Akamai 'Access Denied' 403 to plain curl with a browser UA AND to WebFetch, on robots.txt, sitemap.xml and every HTML path including beta.tucsonaz.gov and the /Departments/Clerks/... legacy paths.

NEW GENERAL TECHNIQUE, WORTH ADDING TO THE REGISTRY: the Akamai block on tucsonaz.gov is defeated for STATIC ASSETS by sending a full browser header set - Accept, Accept-Language, Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site, Upgrade-Insecure-Requests and a same-host Referer - not by the User-Agent alone. With those headers every PDF under /files/sharedassets/public/v/1/... returns HTTP 200. HTML routes stay 403 regardless. So on this host: construct asset URLs, never try to browse. This unlocked the 2019 general canvass, the 2021 primary canvass, the candidate pamphlet and the entire ACFR series.

2019-11-05 sourced from the city's official canvass at /clerks/documents/elections/cot_2019_officialresults_general_11122019.pdf (clean text layer, no OCR needed): Mayor Romero 55,654; W1 Santa Cruz 57,124; W2 Cunningham 59,513; W4 Lee 57,013. The companion ward_total_canvass.pdf IS an image scan and was read with the OCR path (pdftoppm -r 200 -png then tesseract --psm 4); no rotation was needed and the output was clean. It is the Ward 1 sub-report for the same election and is what proves the citywide-election feature.

The Nov 2021 GENERAL canvass PDF could not be located. Swept ~40 constructed filenames across two asset directories and eight plausible canvass dates (the city's own page metadata says it was updated 2021-11-23), plus the 2019 naming convention applied to 2021; all 404. The numeric-id form /clerks/documents/elections/results/{n}.pdf turned out to be RESOLUTION numbers, not election ids - 22970 is the Nov 2018 proposition canvass - and identifying the 2021 canvass resolution would require OCR-sweeping several hundred scanned resolutions, which was refused on budget. Not a hole in the deliverable: all three 2021 seat-holders are sourced at high confidence elsewhere.

THE ACFR ROUTE IS THE BEST SINGLE SOURCE FOR THIS CITY. Tucson publishes a true ACFR with a 'City of Tucson Officials' page naming the mayor and all six ward holders WITH ward labels, as of each June 30. Filenames are inconsistent within the series and must be discovered, not constructed: 2019.pdf, 2020.pdf, 2021.pdf, acfr-2021-2022.pdf, cot-2024-annual-comprehensive-financial-report.pdf, all under /bsd/documents/finance-documents/. FY2023 and FY2025 could not be found under twelve tried naming conventions. All extract cleanly under pdftotext -layout. This single series independently sourced the whole pre-December-2019 roster, the 2021 general-election outcome, and the 2024 Ward 6 appointment. It carries NO vice-mayor annotation, which is why that seat needed a separate and only partly successful hunt.

ACFR STALE-CARRY-OVER CAUGHT: the FY2021 ACFR (as of 2021-06-30) still prints PAUL DURHAM in Ward Three although he resigned 2021-03-01 and Karin Uhlich had held the seat for three months. Recorded per the registry rule that a dated primary record beats the ACFR. DAY-OF-WEEK CHECK CAUGHT A SECOND ERROR: the KOLD story on the Ward 6 appointment says 'On Monday, April 6' - 2024-04-06 was a Saturday; the story was published Monday 2024-05-06, which is the real date. All four December seating dates were day-of-week checked and are Mondays (2019-12-02, 2021-12-06, 2023-12-04, 2025-12-01), consistent with a first-Monday-in-December rule.

Three mid-term changes found and dated, none of which appears in any election result. (1) Ward 3: Paul Durham resigned effective 5 p.m. 2021-03-01; Karin Uhlich appointed the same evening at a special meeting; served to 2021-12-06. (2) Ward 6: Steve Kozachik announced 2024-03-11 he would resign at month end, effective 2024-03-31; seat vacant 34 days; Karin Uhlich appointed unanimously 2024-05-06 - the same person appointed to a second, different ward. (3) Ward 5: Richard Fimbres announced retirement 2025-04-11 for health reasons, effective 2025-05-01; seat vacant 5 days; Rocque Perez appointed and sworn in 2025-05-06 to serve until 2025-12-01. The structural tell was visible in the ACFR diff (FY2022 Kozachik in Ward Six vs FY2024 Uhlich in Ward Six) before any search confirmed it.

Vice Mayor is only partly reconstructed. Sourced: Nikki Lee (observed 2021-07-19 to 2021-12-06), Lane Santa Cruz (from 2021-12-06), Kevin Dahl (observed 2024-01-26 to 2025-01-10), Santa Cruz again (2025 and re-selected for 2026). UNRESOLVED CONTRADICTION, left open rather than smoothed over: a City of Tucson bulletin dated 2025-01-10 is still headed 'Vice Mayor Kevin Dahl', while the Arizona Daily Star's December 2025 report states Santa Cruz won a 'second consecutive year' as vice mayor, which requires her to have held it during 2025. Either the January bulletin is a stale newsletter template or the handover happened after 2025-01-10. Recorded as two rows with Santa Cruz's start set to 2025-01-11 and confidence low. 2019, 2020 and 2023 are filed as gaps.

A.R.S. 9-821.01(D) trap checked from primary evidence and found NOT to apply to Tucson: the August election is a partisan party primary that nominates, not a nonpartisan election that can elect outright. The 2021 primary canvass prints 'DEM Council Member Ward 3' and 'DEM Council Member Ward 5' as separate party contests. No panel seat was decided in August. Unopposed candidates are also not suppressed here (Barajas, Nov 2025, appears with full counts against write-ins only), so an absent seat in Tucson would be genuine missing data. Separately, the Nov 2018 Proposition 408 - which would have moved Tucson to even-year elections and extended sitting terms by a year - was DEFEATED (66,699 yes to 91,513 no), confirmed by OCR of the city's own canvass resolution 22970; the odd-year calendar therefore holds unchanged across 2019-2026.

All 7 seats x 8 years = 56 council/mayor seat-years fully covered; the Vice Mayor tracking seat adds 8 more, of which 5 are covered and 3 are gaps. No 2026 mid-term change was found; Tucson holds no municipal election in even years, so 2026 is a holdover year for all seven seats.
